title: Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulators (TENS)
scope: TENS for chronic, intractable pain other than low back pain (coverage criterion II)

root.label: Chronic pain other than low back pain

children.text: TENS ordered by the treating practitioner for the condition justifying the device

sourceSpan.quote: The practitioner ordering the Transcutaneous Electrical Nerve Stimulators (TENS) unit and related supplies must be the treating practitioner for the disease or condition justifying the need for the TENS unit.

present: {date}: Treating physician prescribes TENS unit for chronic knee osteoarthritis pain.
negated: {date}: TENS unit ordered by a vendor; treating physician not involved.
contradicted: {date}: Order signed by a practitioner who has never treated the patient's pain condition.
paraphrased: {date}: I am the treating physician for this pain condition and am ordering a TENS device.

children.text: Pain present for at least three months

sourceSpan.quote: The pain must have been present for at least three months.

present: {date}: Chronic right knee pain for 8 months, worse with weight bearing.
negated: {date}: Pain onset 3 weeks ago after a fall.
contradicted: {date}: Acute knee pain of 2 weeks duration.
paraphrased: {date}: Knee pain has persisted since last spring (roughly seven months).

children.text: Other appropriate treatment modalities have been tried and failed

sourceSpan.quote: Other appropriate treatment modalities must have been tried and failed.

present: {date}: Completed 8 weeks of physical therapy and scheduled NSAIDs without meaningful relief.
negated: {date}: No prior treatments attempted for this pain.
contradicted: {date}: Pain well controlled with physical therapy; patient satisfied with current regimen.
paraphrased: {date}: Despite a course of PT and anti-inflammatory medication, pain persists.

children.text: Pain etiology is a type accepted as responding to TENS (not headache, visceral, pelvic or TMJ pain)

sourceSpan.quote: The presumed etiology of the pain must be a type that is accepted as responding to TENS therapy.

children.text: Pain being treated is not chronic low back pain
children.suggestedFix: Document the anatomic site of the pain being treated; TENS for chronic low back pain is not covered.

sourceSpan.quote: TENS therapy for Chronic Low Back Pain (CLBP) will be denied as not reasonable and necessary.

present: {date}: TENS is for right knee pain only; patient has no low back pain complaints.
contradicted: {date}: TENS requested for chronic low back pain.

children.text: Trial use for a minimum of one month (30 days), not exceeding two months, monitored by the treating practitioner
children.suggestedFix: Document the TENS rental trial dates and the practitioner's assessment of effectiveness.

sourceSpan.quote: the TENS unit must be used by the beneficiary on a trial basis for a minimum of one month (30 days), but not to exceed two months

present: {date}: 30-day TENS rental trial completed; pain reduced from 7/10 to 4/10, practitioner recommends purchase.
negated: {date}: No trial period; purchase requested directly.
contradicted: {date}: TENS trial lasted 10 days and was discontinued.
paraphrased: {date}: After a month-long supervised trial with the rental unit, the patient reports meaningful benefit.
